items.stem: Which of the following best describes "operations management"?
options: Operations that reduce harm to the environment, such as cutting emissions, waste and resource use
The planning, organizing and controlling of the processes that turn inputs into goods and services
Producing output with the minimum use of resources and cost
The difference between the price of a product and the cost of the bought-in inputs used to make it
items.answer: The planning, organizing and controlling of the processes that turn inputs into goods and services
items.markingKey: B. "operations management" is the planning, organizing and controlling of the processes that turn inputs into goods and services.

items.stem: Explain why higher labour productivity can improve competitiveness.
items.answer: More output per worker lowers labour cost per unit, allowing lower prices or higher margins.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: More output per worker lowers labour cost per unit, allowing lower prices or higher margins. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem:

items.answer: Productivity is important, but operations managers must balance it with quality, flexibility and sustainability.

items.stem: Distinguish between labour productivity and capital productivity.
items.answer: Labour productivity measures output per worker; capital productivity measures output per unit of capital such as machinery.
items.markingKey: Labour productivity measures output per worker; capital productivity measures output per unit of capital such as machinery. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: A bakery produces 3,600 loaves a week with 12 workers. A rival produces 4,000 loaves with 10 workers. Calculate labour productivity for each and suggest one reason for the difference.
items.answer: Bakery: 3,600/12 = 300 loaves per worker; rival: 4,000/10 = 400. The rival may use more automated ovens, better training, or a more efficient layout.
items.markingKey: Bakery: 3,600/12 = 300 loaves per worker; rival: 4,000/10 = 400. The rival may use more automated ovens, better training, or a more efficient layout.

items.stem: Lumen Lighting employs 20 workers, each paid €700 a week, producing 2,100 units a week. After new equipment is installed, output rises by 25% and the workforce stays at 20. Calculate labour productivity and labour cost per unit before and after the change.
items.answer: Before: 105.0 units per worker, labour cost €6.67 per unit. After: output 2,625, productivity 131.3 units per worker (+25.0%), labour cost €5.33 per unit.
